## What / why
The owner answered #376 on 2026-09-23: **"No real circuits."**

ADR-0020 §7.2 made capturing a corpus of real version-1 documents a **hard precondition** on §7.5d (deleting `serialize.ts`) and on C.1 — with an exit clause if none exist, precisely so the precondition could not block the switch silently. The exit now applies.

This records it as **L-001** in a new *Stated limits* section of `docs/development/observed-bugs.md`, which is where §7.2 says it must go. A limit recorded there is not a bug — it is something the project knows it cannot evidence, written down so a later reader does not mistake the absence of a finding for the absence of a problem.

## The limit, stated plainly
The eleven cases in the #328 spike were constructed by **reading `serialize.ts`'s writer**, so they cannot contain anything the writer's *observed* output would have had but its code does not obviously produce — a stale `crossesWireIds`, an arc segment, an orphaned junction, a `'bus'` endpoint in an unexpected combination, a multi-driven pin. A real save could have carried a shape none of them has, and now none ever will.

**Nothing is blocked and nothing needs re-deciding.** But the importer's parity evidence (N.2, #377) now rests entirely on documents written by the same reasoning that will write the importer — the classic weak-oracle shape. The mitigation was already in the plan and simply matters more now: the **held-out oracle** — the official nand2tetris vectors (#193) and the differential harness against `web-ide`'s reference simulator (#338), neither of which HACER authored.

## Verification
`pnpm run lint:docs` — exit 0. Docs-only; `test:run` and `build` left to CI.

Closes the §7.2 precondition. #376 closes with this PR.
